definitions.gloss: holding an item; reservation of goods; setting aside
definitions.explanation: the practice of a store holding an item for a customer to purchase later; reserving merchandise before payment

examples.japanese: この{商品|しょうひん}の{取|と}り{置|お}きをお{願|ねが}いできますか。
examples.english: Could you hold this item for me?

examples.japanese: {取|と}り{置|お}きは{三日間|みっかかん}まで{可能|かのう}です。
examples.english: We can hold items for up to three days.

examples.japanese: {電話|でんわ}で{取|と}り{置|お}きを{頼|たの}んでおいた{本|ほん}を{取|と}りに{来|き}た。
examples.english: I came to pick up the book I had asked them to hold over the phone.

notes:
FORMS:
{取|と}り{置|お}く (to set aside, to hold) → {取|と}り{置|お}き (noun form)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {取|と}り{置|お}きをする (to hold an item)
- {取|と}り{置|お}きを{頼|たの}む (to ask for an item to be held)
- {取|と}り{置|お}き{期間|きかん} (holding period)

SHOPPING CONTEXT:
Many Japanese stores offer {取|と}り{置|お}き service, allowing customers to reserve items for a limited period before purchasing. This is common in bookstores, clothing stores, and specialty shops.

RELATED WORDS:
- {取|と}り{寄|よ}せ (ordering in, special order)
- {予約|よやく} (reservation - broader term)

cross_references.headword: {購入予約|こうにゅうよやく}
